summary:
TerraShaft is a web application designed to help farmers and Agricultural Extension Officers (Penyuluh Pertanian Lapangan / PPL) build adaptive crop rotation scenarios based on satellite observations, weather data, soil moisture, topography, soil characteristics, and local agricultural context.

The system transforms complex geospatial data into easy-to-understand crop rotation recommendations, complete with water requirement estimates, soil health indicators, drought risk assessments, crop alternatives, and the scientific rationale behind each recommendation.
details:
Project Name: TerraShaft — Adaptive Crop Rotation & Soil Regeneration

TerraShaft is a global decision-support system for climate-aware agriculture, crop rotation, and soil regeneration. It connects NASA climate data, soil properties, elevation, agroecological zoning, and localized cultivar information to help users design more practical crop rotation plans for a selected location.

Users can enter a coordinate, search for a place, or select a regional preset. TerraShaft retrieves climate and soil information, estimates reference evapotranspiration, available water capacity, soil moisture conditions, and agroecological characteristics, then evaluates multiple four-period crop rotation sequences. The system ranks possible pathways according to water constraints, soil regeneration goals, crop compatibility, cultivar availability, and projected economic outcomes.

The main benefit is that TerraShaft translates complex Earth observation and environmental datasets into understandable agricultural recommendations. Instead of providing only a single crop suggestion, the system presents multiple ranked pathways and explains the reasoning behind each recommendation. This can help farmers, agricultural extension officers, researchers, and policymakers make more informed decisions under changing rainfall patterns and increasing water stress.

The desired impact is to support more resilient rainfed and dryland agriculture, reduce dependence on rigid historical planting calendars, improve soil management, encourage diversified crop rotations, and make scientific environmental data more accessible at field level. TerraShaft also includes transparent fallbacks and provenance indicators so users can distinguish live data, static registries, knowledge resources, reference standards, and planned integrations.

The project was developed using TypeScript, React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, Typst, and web-based mapping components. The application uses NASA POWER for agroclimate variables, ISRIC SoilGrids for soil properties, Nominatim and OpenStreetMap for location search, and Open-Meteo Elevation for elevation-related inputs. The live application is supported by structured local crop and cultivar registries, agroecological rules, crop compatibility logic, and a rotation optimization engine.

TerraShaft is creative because it combines environmental observation, soil intelligence, agroecological zoning, cultivar localization, and crop rotation optimization in a single explainable workflow. The system does not fabricate cultivar names or seed availability when a region is not covered. Instead, it uses transparent species-level fallback logic and clearly communicates the limitations of its recommendations. The team considered data availability, geographic coverage, uncertainty, regional cultivar differences, soil variability, water constraints, explainability, and the need to validate digital recommendations with local agronomists and field observations.
